children: , the integrated oil-and-gas producer, edged approximately 0.2% higher to $165.49 Friday as the International Energy Agency projected a growing global supply deficit. That gain stood out as Brent and West Texas Intermediate fell more than 3% during a turbulent session.

The IEA forecasts that worldwide supply will shrink by 5.7 million barrels per day, or roughly 6%, in 2026. Inventories drained at a daily pace of 3.1 million barrels in August, and normal Gulf production may not return before 2027. That backdrop favors major producers capable of delivering reliable barrels beyond the hardest-hit regions.

Exxon produced $23.6 billion in operating cash flow during the second quarter and deployed $6.8 billion toward cash capital expenditures, leaving a $16.8 billion gap before dividends, financing and other uses. The picture adds a valuation warning: the $165.49 share price sits 29.86% above the $127.43 GF Value estimate. Scarce supply could strengthen Exxon's cash machine, but the valuation premium and Friday's abrupt oil reversal leave little room for a softer crude market.

title: Exxon Edged Higher as IEA Sees a 5.7 Million-Barrel Supply Drop
